evals.prompt: Reverse engineer how Lovable grew. We're an early-revenue AI app builder and want to copy what worked.
evals.expected_output: Should check for product-marketing.md first and confirm the window, country, data tools, connected data, and budget cap before paid calls. Should build the spine first: run the bundled script (site, stack, history, ads), build traffic.csv from one vendor and moves.csv, and mark the inflection. Should read the funnel stage by stage (acquisition channels, activation, revenue with pricing history, referral loops such as a 'made with' badge confirmed by anchor data, hiring). Should run the moves analysis, credit clusters, and say timing isn't proof. Should compare with the user's own data like with like. Should deliver ranked plays filtered for early revenue, each naming the skill that runs it and the loop that sustains it, with a paste-ready prompt, plus plays to skip and the one play to start this week.
assertions: Checks for product-marketing.md
Confirms window, data tools, and budget cap before paid calls
Uses the bundled teardown script for free evidence
Labels findings Observed, Inferred, or Not found with links
Uses one traffic vendor for the whole curve and marks an inflection
Looks for a product loop through badges or anchor data
States that moves lining up with growth is not proof of cause
Each play names the skill that runs it and includes a paste-ready prompt
Includes plays to skip, filtered by the user's stage

evals.prompt: What content works for Notion on YouTube and TikTok? I just want their thumbnail and hook patterns, nothing about their overall growth.
evals.expected_output: Should run Content mode only: collect official handles, then pull up to 100 posts from the last 180 days per channel via ScrapeCreators or Apify. Should skip posts under 10 days old, rank within each channel only, split into thirds with code, and call no pattern under 24 settled posts. Should download and open thumbnails and covers in the same run and mark undownloaded images as not read. Should report counted traits for top vs bottom thirds, house style with hex colors, and fill-in formulas with real examples. Should not run traffic, ads, or backlink stages.
assertions: Runs Content mode, skipping traffic, ads, and link stages
Ranks posts within a channel, not across channels
Compares the top third with the bottom third
Downloads and opens images rather than describing them from captions
Gives fill-in formulas with a real example each
Calls no pattern when a channel has fewer than 24 settled posts

evals.prompt: My competitor's traffic tripled in March right after their founder tweeted their revenue. So the tweet caused it, right? Build me a plan around posting revenue tweets.
evals.expected_output: Should not accept the causal claim. Should check what else happened around March: funding, press, launches, ad network starts (pixel first-seen from the stack command), a product loop, a category-wide surge (check peers). Should cluster moves less than a month apart and credit the cluster, not one move. Should compare brand-search growth to visit growth. Should label the founder's revenue figure as reported. Should present revenue posting as a candidate play with its evidence strength, and filter it by whether the user has numbers worth sharing and an audience.
assertions: Does not treat timing as proof of cause
Checks other moves and confounders around the same month
Clusters overlapping moves rather than crediting one
Labels founder-stated revenue as reported
Frames the tweet play as a candidate with stated evidence strength

evals.prompt: Do a growth teardown of acme-analytics.com but sign up for their trial and go through onboarding so we can see the emails they send.
evals.expected_output: Should decline to create an account in the target's product, explaining that the teardown uses public evidence only. Should offer public alternatives: their onboarding docs, getting-started pages, changelog, public help center, Wayback snapshots, and reviews or posts where users describe onboarding. Should suggest the user do a signup themselves under their own judgment if they want the emails, and should proceed with the rest of the teardown.
assertions: Does not create an account or fill in forms on the target's product
Offers public sources for onboarding evidence
Continues the teardown with public evidence

evals.prompt: Quick scan: how does Granola get customers? I have a call with a prospect in their space in an hour and $1 of budget.
evals.expected_output: Should run Quick mode within the budget, favoring free sources: the bundled script's site, stack, history, and ads commands, Google Trends for brand interest if paid traffic data doesn't fit the cap, and headline funnel findings. Should deliver a one-page brief: the curve, top moves, and five plays routed to skills, with dated estimates and method notes listing what was skipped.
assertions: Uses quick scan mode
Prioritizes free sources to stay within the budget
Dates every number and labels estimates
Delivers a one-page output with a few plays
Lists skipped steps or unavailable data in method notes

evals.prompt: We did a teardown of Acme last month. Check what they've done since and tell me if anything matters.
evals.expected_output: Should run Watch mode: rerun the stack, history, and site commands, check the ad libraries, and pull the last month's posts into a fresh moves log, then diff it against the previous log with the script's diff command. Should report only meaningful new moves (new ad network, page family, loop, pricing change, content format, hiring burst), or 'no new moves'. For each, should say whether it changes a play and which skill to hand it to, and should mention scheduling it as the growth-move watch loop in marketing-loops.
assertions: Runs Watch mode against the previous move log
Uses the script's diff command
Reports only meaningful new moves or 'no new moves'
Says which skill each new move should go to
Mentions scheduling via the marketing-loops growth-move watch loop

evals.prompt: Compare us (we have GA4 and Search Console connected) to how Linear grew. Our GA4 shows 40K visits a month and Similarweb says Linear has 2M.
evals.expected_output: Should not compare GA4 numbers with a Similarweb estimate. Should put Linear's estimate next to the same vendor's estimate of the user's domain, then use Search Console and GA4 for depth: which of Linear's winning page families the user has and their impressions, the user's channel mix and signup conversion. Should fill a gap table by funnel stage and turn the biggest gaps into plays routed to skills.
assertions: Refuses to compare GA4 visits with a third-party estimate
Uses the same vendor for both domains
Uses Search Console and GA4 for depth on the user's side
Fills a gap table by funnel stage
Turns gaps into plays routed to skills
